dedupe_keys.name: port of rotterdam smart infrastructure programme sensor satellite and ai asset management

description: This case describes how the Port of Rotterdam Authority, which manages a port area of more than 12,500 hectares and owns about 89 kilometres of quay walls, is making its physical assets smart. The authority uses sensors to report asset condition in real time, for example on waste containers and sewer gullies, and combines its data with that of stakeholders to plan work and inspections. The Machine Learning Inspector project aims to automate frequent manual inspections with sensors and artificial intelligence. Because dredging costs on average about 10 percent of terminal availability, the Plato planning tool combines quay wall inspection, dredging and depth survey planning with terminal planning to cut downtime and emissions. Satellites survey the whole port every 11 to 22 days to detect quay wall displacement, with tilt sensors giving hourly positions where risk is higher, and the WindLASS project uses LiDAR wind measurements to estimate the wind load of larger cranes on quay structures. A pilot reused dredged sediment for flood protection. Coverage: one port, programme page dated September 2022. Access: free web page. Licence and cost: free to read, no open licence. Caveats: a descriptive page without performance figures, and the underlying data and tools are internal. It illustrates digital twin and resilience-oriented asset management of port infrastructure. It relates to the Port of Rotterdam flood adaptation strategy and the World Port Index in the catalogue.
